MPE Bender  (Windows 64-bit VST3)
by prodcoldie
================================================
(the version is in the zip's filename / the plugin's Settings tab)

What it is
----------
An instrument plugin that hosts your own synth (Serum 2, Vital, Pigments, ...)
inside it and drives it from a built-in piano roll where every note carries its
own pitch curve. Each note goes out on its own MPE channel, so the bends are
independent per note - draw a note that slides from one key to another while
other notes hold steady, add sine/triangle vibrato per note, etc.


Requirements
------------
- Windows 10/11, 64-bit
- A VST3 host (FL Studio, Ableton Live, Reaper, Bitwig, Cubase, Studio One, ...)
- Your own VST3 synth to put inside it. For the per-note bends to be truly
  independent the synth needs an "MPE" mode (Serum 2, Vital, Pigments, Massive X,
  Diva, Repro, Surge XT, Ableton stock instruments, and most modern synths have it).


Install
-------
1. Copy the folder

       MPE Bender.vst3

   into

       C:\Program Files\Common Files\VST3\

   (You may need to click "Continue" for administrator permission. That folder is
   where every DAW looks for VST3 plugins.)

2. In your DAW, rescan / refresh plugins:
     - FL Studio:  Options > Manage plugins > "Find installed plugins"
     - Ableton:    Preferences > Plug-Ins > Rescan
     - Reaper:     Preferences > VST > Re-scan
     - others:     the plugin manager / preferences has a "rescan" button

3. Add "MPE Bender" to a track AS AN INSTRUMENT (not an audio effect).
   Manufacturer shows as "YourStudio", category Instrument / Synth.


Using it
--------
1. Open MPE Bender's window. Use the synth menu on the toolbar:
   "Load new synth..." -> pick your synth's .vst3 (it'll offer to save it to the
   menu with a name, so next time it's one click). A fresh instance also tries to
   auto-load the last synth you used.

2. Click "Open synth" to show your synth's own window. Turn ON its MPE mode and
   set its pitch-bend range to match "Pitch-bend range" on MPE Bender's Settings
   tab (default 48 semitones). Without MPE the synth still plays, but all its
   notes share one bend instead of bending independently.

3. Draw notes in the roll. Basics:
     b / s            switch Draw / Select tools
     drag a note body   move it;  drag its right edge   length + tail bend
     Ctrl+click / dbl-click a note   add a bend point;  drag points to shape it
     select one note    a shape wheel appears (straight / sine / triangle) with
                        cycles / skew / start+end amplitude controls
     right-click        deselect;  right-click + drag   erase notes
     Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V   undo / copy / paste
     M                  mute / unmute selected notes
     middle-drag        pan;  Ctrl+scroll   zoom
   Scale menu on the toolbar highlights a scale in the roll.

4. Press play in your DAW. MPE Bender loops its own pattern (Loop bars on the
   toolbar), synced to the host tempo, and plays your synth with the per-note
   bends. Project state saves your synth choice + its patch.


Updates
-------
Settings tab > Updates. If the person who built this hosted an update feed it
will check on startup and offer to self-install on the next DAW restart. If it
says "Auto-update not configured", just ask them for a new zip.


Troubleshooting
---------------
- Doesn't show up after rescan: make sure you copied the FULL "MPE Bender.vst3"
  folder (not just a file inside it) into C:\Program Files\Common Files\VST3\, and
  that you rescanned. Some DAWs need you to add that path in their VST3 settings.
- Notes bend together instead of independently: the hosted synth isn't in MPE
  mode, or its pitch-bend range doesn't match MPE Bender's.
- Crash on load / "missing DLL": this build has the runtime baked in, but if a
  very old Windows still complains, install "Microsoft Visual C++ 2015-2022
  Redistributable (x64)" from Microsoft.
